$comment: Provenance and trust level of every design reference.
`size` is the section's size in Figma design px and is the authority for the
aspect-ratio check in scripts/verify-design.mjs. Where `sizeFrom` is
"reference", it is the reference PNG's own aspect scaled to `designWidth` —
i.e. the screenshot is trusted for shape. Where `sizeFrom` is "figma-badge",
it is the size Figma itself printed next to the selected node in a capture,
`blockCheck` says whether the PNG beside this entry is trustworthy enough to
compare content against. Saying so here is what keeps the verifier honest: a
reference nobody has vouched for must not be able to pass a section, and must
not be able to fail one either. Every `false` and every loosened tolerance
carries its reason, and a low score on a section that is mostly background is
weak evidence — noted where it applies rather than quietly banked.
Node ids are deliberately absent. The capture script's TARGETS table is the
one place that maps a node id to an output file, and three of its declared
node sizes were wrong — which is the whole reason this file exists. Restating
ids here would add a second unverified copy of the thing that broke.

LogoCloud.blockToleranceReason: Six logos at 60% opacity on white: nearly the whole frame is background, so a sub-pixel placement difference moves the score far more than the amount of ink on the page justifies. By the same token a low score here is weak evidence of fidelity.

CenteredCta.blockToleranceReason: Captured through the Playwright viewer at 2x rather than exported by Figma, so it carries a little canvas around the node; the composition is intact and worth comparing against.

Footer.blockToleranceReason: Re-captured. The first attempt declared this node as 1200x519, matched no blob that size, and wrote out a strip containing Figma's own selection badge, the canvas behind the frame, and a cookie banner. That badge read '1200 Fill x 250 Hug', which is where `size` comes from and what the re-capture used. The reference is now the real footer. Caveat: this section is almost entirely white, so its low block score is weak evidence — and the reference shows the copyright at the left and 'All Rights Reserved' at the right, which the build deliberately renders as one field (see docs/decisions/0005). The block check is too coarse to see that difference; do not read a pass here as agreement on it.
